chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out before the dawn prayer, and with him was a piece of bread which he had dipped in milk, and he was eating while walking, while Bilal was calling the Adhan for prayer, so he prayed with the people.

key_terms.بِلَالٌ: Bilal ibn Rabah, the companion known for calling the Adhan
key_terms.فَصَلَّى بِالنَّاسِ: He led the people in prayer
key_terms.كِسْرَةٌ: A piece or fragment of bread

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet (SAWW) do while eating before the dawn prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Prophet’s (SAWW) ease and lack of rigidity in daily conduct, specifically demonstrating the permissibility of eating while walking and during the Adhan period. It serves as a practical legal precedent (hujjah) in Shia jurisprudence for the validity of prayer and general acts of worship performed while in motion or consuming food, reflecting the Sunnah’s adaptability to human needs.
